Investigation complete — 3 read-only calls used, all succeeded. Both named objects were found and are configuration-healthy; the failure signal is runtime-level at the model route. Here is my draft issue:

<issue>
## Summary
Alert `AgentModelRouteFailing` (severity critical) reports that agent `demo-worker` in namespace `kagent` ended its last run with TASK_STATE_FAILED after receiving HTTP 429 "Too Many Requests" from its model route, ModelConfig `demo-stub-429`. I inspected both named objects; the kagent configuration itself is healthy and the failure appears to be coming from the model backend at runtime.

## Dedupe key
ov-demo-worker-429

## What is failing
- Agent `demo-worker` (namespace `kagent`): sessions ending TASK_STATE_FAILED when the model route returns 429, per the alert annotation.
- ModelConfig `demo-stub-429` (namespace `kagent`): provider OpenAI, model `demo-stub`, baseUrl `http://model-stub.guard-demo.svc.cluster.local:8080/v1`, secret ref `demo-stub-key`/`api-key`, maxTokens 200, timeout 30, stream true.
- Observed state: the Agent CRD shows all conditions True (Accepted, EgressPoliciesApplied, ResolvedRefs, Compatible, Ready) with observedGeneration 7 and no events. The ModelConfig shows Accepted=True and ResolvedRefs=True (referenced secret resolves). So config/references are fine — the 429 is generated by the `model-stub` endpoint in namespace `guard-demo` at request time.

## Likely cause
Not fully established from the cluster objects alone. The configuration is valid and all references resolve, so the failure is runtime: the stub model server at `model-stub.guard-demo.svc.cluster.local:8080` is returning 429 Too Many Requests. Two plausible explanations a human should distinguish: (a) the stub backend is genuinely rate-limiting or rejecting the API key/quota; or (b) this is an intentional demo fixture — the ModelConfig is named `demo-stub-429` and both objects carry the label `guard-demo=true`, which suggests a deliberately failing stub used to exercise this alerting/self-healing flow. I could not verify the stub server's behavior or the agent session logs because the alert names no pod and agents run as sessions, not pods.

## Recommendation
A human should check the `model-stub` service/deployment in namespace `guard-demo` and its logs to confirm why it returns 429 (rate limit, quota, or intentional fixture), and verify the key in secret `demo-stub-key` is what the stub expects. If the fixture is intentional, silence or label-exclude `guard-demo=true` alerts. If unintentional, raise/relax the stub's rate limit or add client-side retry with exponential backoff for 429s in the model route. One improvement to the agent setup: ModelConfig status conditions only cover config resolution, not endpoint health — surface per-request model-route errors (e.g., an endpoint-health condition or rate-limit counter) so 429s are visible without waiting for a failed session. Nothing has been changed or fixed by this investigation.

## Needs a human
Yes
</issue>
